# When Support Foot Zero Velocity Constraint Continuously Violates in OCS2 Full-Body NMPC, What Should Be Changed First?

> **Current answer:** Confirm whether the constraint is written as an equality only dependent on state; community suggests rewriting it as a state-input equality and avoiding hard-penalizing residual errors. When gradient calculations are large, evaluate the analytical derivative of Pinocchio.

## Key terms

- Whole-Body Control (WBC) (全身控制)
- Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) (非线性模型预测控制)
- Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) (顺序二次规划)
- Contact Constraint (接触约束)

## Problem and symptoms

- Support foot zero velocity constraint is violated during standing and small running.
- Support foot continues to slip, some runs directly crash.

## Environment

- OCS2, Pinocchio, full-body NMPC, state is q and ν, input is ground reaction force and joint torque.

## Priority diagnostics

- Distinguish between pure-state equality constraints and state-input equality constraints, then verify SQP solver support range.

## Possible causes

- Writing the foot zero velocity as a pure-state equality constraint, but the solver path cannot directly handle it.

## Attempts

- Original author tried constraint observer and penalty methods, but slipping still exists.

## Effective fixes

- Community suggests changing the constraint to the acceleration layer's end, making it a state-input equality constraint.

## Result

- Response provides direction for re-implementation, but original author did not post final experimental results in the Issue.

## Limitations

- Conclusion is based on community practice; response also states the judgment on OCS2 SQP capability is based on previous version, should re-check current version.

## Safety notes

- Before real machine testing, check foot end constraint residuals and friction margin to avoid bringing simulation slippage into hardware.

## Image and visual evidence

- Issue includes screenshot of foot end constraint observer and slippage video; this round only confirms the phenomenon based on the author's text description, and specific numerical values have not been pixel-by-pixel verified.

## Applicability boundary

- Applicable to OCS2 full-body NMPC using q and ν as state and SQP solver; other solvers need to re-verify constraint support.
